---
title: "Limitations and Negative Evidence"
---

The v0.1.0 codebook is locked for the manual pilot, not for final publication
claims. It does not approve substantive findings about Germany, Koenigsberg, or
any comparison case.

The Germany-first corpus is a mechanism-discovery sequence. It must not become
a confirmation path for inherited interpretations. Negative evidence and rival
explanations are first-class records, including successful discharge, veteran
protection, contribution reclassification, absent expected rhetoric, coercion
without debt, debt without coercion, explicit rejection, chronology
contradiction, and actor inconsistency.

Absence claims require a documented search scope. Rhetoric alone does not prove
reception, and rhetoric or reception alone does not prove policy causation.

The following remain provisional: reliability thresholds, whether etic-only
evidence can support strong published claims, the approval rule for decisive
evidence, reception-evidence minimums, policy-causation minimums, translation
authority, and source storage or external model-processing policy.
